meta.name: Frontend Product Builder Form Field Control Components
meta.description: Canonical specialized form controls for boolean choices, exclusive choices, bounded selections, multiline text, and date-related values.

CheckboxField.name: CheckboxField
CheckboxField.description: Canonical boolean or explicitly approved tri-state form field with a clickable label, supporting description, validation, eligibility explanation, and consent-aware behavior.
capabilities: Collect one independent boolean value.
Represent checked, unchecked, and explicitly approved indeterminate states.
Present consent, acknowledgement, preference, and feature-option choices.
Associate the control with visible label, description, and validation feedback.
Explain disabled or unavailable eligibility without relying on a tooltip.
Preserve native checkbox semantics and keyboard interaction.

foundation.source: Radix Checkbox or native checkbox, Label, FieldHelp, FieldError
foundation.reason: Checkbox fields require specialized control-label composition, full-label activation, consent policy, indeterminate semantics, validation association, and disabled-reason handling.

boolean.intent: Collect an ordinary independent true or false value.
allowedUse: Choose whether a secondary behavior applies.
prohibitedUse: Choosing one option from a mutually exclusive set.
Triggering an immediate destructive action.
Representing an unknown value without an approved tri-state contract.

consent.intent: Collect explicit informed consent for a policy, declaration, or consequential agreement.
allowedUse: Accept terms required for the current workflow.
Confirm authorization to perform an operation.
Provide explicit data-processing consent where the product policy requires it.
prohibitedUse: Preselected consent.
Bundling unrelated consent statements.
Hiding material policy text behind a tooltip.
Using one checkbox for several legally or operationally distinct agreements.

acknowledgement.intent: Require the user to confirm that a consequence or condition has been understood.
allowedUse: Confirm understanding before a sensitive operation.
Acknowledge that an operation is irreversible.
Confirm review of a required warning.
prohibitedUse: Replacing a ConfirmationDialog for a destructive action.
Using generic wording without naming the consequence.

triState.intent: Represent an explicit three-state domain value or hierarchical selection.
allowedUse: Hierarchical selection with partially selected descendants.
Domain value whose contract explicitly distinguishes yes, no, and unspecified.
prohibitedUse: Using indeterminate only as a visual effect.
Submitting indeterminate without a defined domain mapping.
Ordinary consent.
Mutually exclusive option selection.

compact.intent: Dense independent option inside a compact operational form or filter region.

default.intent: Ordinary checkbox field with label and optional description.

comfortable.intent: High-attention acknowledgement or consent with longer supporting content.

slots.name: control
slots.description: The native or approved checkbox control.
contentRestrictions: The control must expose native-equivalent checked, unchecked, disabled, required, and indeterminate semantics.
The visual indicator must not be the only source of state.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Visible statement describing the independent choice.
contentRestrictions: Write the label as a clear state or agreement.
Avoid vague labels such as Ativar without naming what will be enabled.
Consent wording must identify the agreement.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Optional persistent explanation, consequence, or eligibility context.
contentRestrictions: Material consequences remain visible.
Supplementary policy details may use a clearly labeled link.
The description must not contain unrelated choices.

slots.name: requiredIndicator
slots.description: Optional localized required-choice indication.
contentRestrictions: Required state must also exist in validation and control semantics.
Required consent must begin unchecked.

slots.name: disabledReason
slots.description: Optional visible explanation of why the choice cannot be changed.
contentRestrictions: Required when the reason is not otherwise obvious.
Do not expose internal capability keys.

slots.name: error
slots.description: Current normalized checkbox-field validation error.
contentRestrictions: Required-checkbox errors explain the required acknowledgement or choice.
Raw schema messages are prohibited.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable checkbox identity associated with its label and descriptive content.
restrictions: Must remain unique and stable.

props.name: name
restrictions: Must map to one boolean or approved tri-state field.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Consent and acknowledgement variants require purpose-specific content.
Tri-state requires an explicit domain mapping.

props.name: size
restrictions: Compact must not reduce the usable target below the design-system minimum.

props.name: checked
restrictions: Indeterminate is valid only for triState.
Consent must not be initialized as checked unless a specific lawful and product-approved policy explicitly permits it.

props.name: onCheckedChange
restrictions: The callback updates form state but does not perform a consequential mutation directly.

props.name: required
props.description: Indicates that the active form contract requires the checked state or an explicit value.
restrictions: Required semantics must match the validation schema.
Required does not imply default checked.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Indicates that the value cannot currently be changed.
restrictions: The disabled reason must be available when not obvious.
Disabled and read-only presentation must not be conflated.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Indicates that the current checkbox value violates the active form contract.
restrictions: Invalid state requires an associated normalized error.

spacingOwnership: CheckboxField owns spacing among control, label, description, disabled reason, and error.
The form layout owns spacing among sibling fields.
The clickable label region includes the control and primary label without including unrelated links.
composition.surfaceOwnership: CheckboxField owns no surface by default. High-attention acknowledgement may use a subtle semantic region supplied by the parent workflow.
rules: One CheckboxField represents one independent boolean or approved tri-state value.
Mutually exclusive choices require RadioGroupField.
Consent begins unchecked by default.
Indeterminate requires an explicit submitted-value policy.
A checkbox must not execute a destructive operation immediately upon checking.
The label and control form one clear activation target.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for independent boolean values and explicit acknowledgements.
Remember-device or session preferences must state their effect clearly.
Feature toggles, inheritance, and acknowledgements require capability-aware state.
Use for required declarations or review acknowledgements, not for the final decision itself.
Use for independent binary filters when the meaning remains clear.

prohibited: Reading form context without an approved adapter.

notes: The owning form controls the checked value, validation, touched state, dirty state, and submission mapping.
Hierarchical selection logic remains in the owning feature.
The field emits value changes only.
Policy links retain their own explicit navigation behavior.

responsive.strategy: Preserve the complete label, consequence, and validation content beside or below a consistently positioned control.
responsive.compact: Align the control to the start of the first label line. Supporting content wraps beneath the label.
responsive.wide: Keep readable line length for consent and acknowledgement text.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not stretch legal or operational text across the route.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Labels, descriptions, reasons, and errors wrap without page overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: The control, label, links, and error remain operable and associated at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: native checkbox or equivalent checkbox role with associated visible label
keyboard: Space toggles the checkbox when eligible.
Tab moves focus to the checkbox once.
Links inside supporting content remain separately operable.
Indeterminate state follows approved checkbox keyboard behavior.
focus: Clicking the associated label toggles the control.
Validation does not reset the current value.
announcements: Checked, unchecked, and mixed states are exposed.
Required and invalid state are perceivable.
Disabled reason is programmatically associated when necessary.
aria: Use native checked semantics where possible.
Use aria-checked=mixed only for approved indeterminate state.
Use aria-describedby for description, disabled reason, and error.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Checked, mixed, invalid, disabled, required, and consent meaning use text, shape, and semantics in addition to color.

content.minimum: One checkbox and one clear visible label.
content.typical: Control, label, optional description, and conditional validation error.
content.maximum: One coherent agreement or independent choice with concise supporting content.
content.wrapping: Labels and descriptions wrap naturally while the control remains aligned to the first line.
content.truncation: Consent, acknowledgement, and validation text must not be truncated.
content.localization: Support expanded labels, policy links, required wording, and validation messages.
content.emptyBehavior: A CheckboxField without a label is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Raw boolean field names, capability keys, policy IDs, and backend enum values are prohibited.

notes: A group of independent checkboxes may be composed by a feature-owned fieldset, but each CheckboxField still owns one independent value.
Bulk table selection uses the DataTable selection contract rather than CheckboxField.

RadioGroupField.name: RadioGroupField
RadioGroupField.description: Canonical exclusive-choice field for selecting exactly one value from a small, visible, stable set of mutually exclusive options.
capabilities: Collect one value from a mutually exclusive option set.
Present options as stacked, inline, or descriptive-card choices.
Associate the complete option set with a visible legend.
Expose option descriptions and disabled reasons.
Support native-equivalent arrow-key navigation.
Represent required, invalid, disabled, and read-only group states.

foundation.source: Radix Radio Group or native radio controls, fieldset, legend, FieldHelp, FieldError
foundation.reason: Exclusive choices require fieldset-level semantics, one shared legend, option-level labels, arrow-key interaction, disabled-option policy, and responsive option composition.

stacked.intent: Present options vertically for reliable scanning, descriptions, or narrow containers.
prohibitedUse: Large dynamic option sets.
Dozens of values.
Options requiring remote search.

inline.intent: Present a very small set of short, familiar choices on one wrapping line.
allowedUse: Yes or no when a checkbox would not communicate the semantics correctly.
prohibitedUse: Options with descriptions.
Long localized labels.
More options than remain immediately scannable.
Compact layout where controls become crowded.

cards.intent: Present a small set of consequential options requiring a title, description, and optional supporting metadata.
prohibitedUse: Decorative card selection.
More than a small bounded set.
Options that are not mutually exclusive.
Using card layout only to make an ordinary choice appear premium.

compact.intent: Dense set of short exclusive options.

comfortable.intent: Consequential or descriptive options requiring more reading space.

slots.name: legend
slots.description: Visible group question or field label.
contentRestrictions: The legend must communicate the decision represented by the complete option set.
Do not repeat the same label inside every option.

slots.name: requiredIndicator
slots.description: Optional localized required-choice indication.
contentRestrictions: Required state must also exist in validation semantics.

slots.name: help
slots.description: Optional persistent guidance applying to the complete option set.
contentRestrictions: Explain the decision criteria or scope.
Option-specific content belongs with the option.

slots.name: option
slots.description: One mutually exclusive selectable option.
contentRestrictions: Every option requires a stable value and visible label.
Options must be mutually exclusive.
Raw backend enum values are prohibited.

slots.name: optionLabel
slots.description: Visible user-facing option label.
contentRestrictions: Labels should allow direct comparison among options.
Avoid ambiguous labels such as Standard or Advanced without context.

slots.name: optionDescription
slots.description: Optional explanation of one option's effect, eligibility, or trade-off.
contentRestrictions: Descriptions must remain concise.
Material differences among options should remain visible.

slots.name: optionDisabledReason
slots.description: Optional visible reason one option cannot be selected.
contentRestrictions: Required when the reason is not obvious.
Do not expose capability IDs or policy internals.

slots.name: error
slots.description: Current normalized group validation error.
contentRestrictions: The error applies to the complete choice group.
Do not repeat the same group error after every option.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable group identity used by legend, descriptions, and errors.
restrictions: Must be unique and stable.

props.name: name
props.description: Stable form name shared by the mutually exclusive options.
restrictions: All options in the group represent one form value.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Inline is limited to a very small set of short labels.
Cards require meaningful descriptive content.

props.name: size
restrictions: Compact must retain minimum target size and readable option association.

props.name: value
restrictions: Value must match one eligible normalized option or null before selection.
Do not store visible labels as unstable values.

props.name: onValueChange
restrictions: The callback updates form state and does not execute the final workflow action.

props.name: options
restrictions: Options require unique values and user-facing labels.
Large or remotely searched option sets require SelectField or a dedicated combobox.
Option order follows user decision logic rather than backend enumeration.

props.name: required
props.description: Indicates that one option must be selected.
restrictions: Must remain synchronized with the validation schema.

props.name: disabled
restrictions: Group-level disabled reason must be visible when not obvious.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Indicates that the current selection violates the active form contract.
restrictions: Invalid state requires a group-level error.

spacingOwnership: RadioGroupField owns spacing among legend, help, options, option descriptions, disabled reasons, and error.
Each option owns spacing between its control, label, and supporting description.
The form layout owns spacing around the complete field.
composition.surfaceOwnership: Stacked and inline variants own no surface. Cards variant owns one selectable option surface per option without adding another card around the complete group.
rules: One group represents one mutually exclusive value.
The complete field uses one legend.
Few visible options favor radio controls over a select.
Large or searchable option sets require another control.
Option values are normalized before reaching the shared component.
Disabled options retain understandable visible context.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for small, stable, mutually exclusive option sets.
Decision options must remain distinct from machine recommendations.
Use for configuration modes and bounded policy choices.
Use only when authentication requires a genuine exclusive option.
Use for a very small exclusive filter set; larger sets use SelectField.

notes: The owning form controls the selected value, validation, touched state, dirty state, and submission mapping.
The owning feature resolves option eligibility and content.
The group emits selection changes only.
The foundation manages native-equivalent option focus movement.

responsive.strategy: Preserve visible comparison among options while transforming inline choices into stacked choices before labels or targets become crowded.
responsive.compact: Use stacked presentation. Card options become full width.
responsive.medium: Use stacked or a short wrapping inline group.
responsive.wide: Use the selected variant while preserving readable option widths.
responsive.ultrawide: Constrain descriptive cards rather than stretching them across the route.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Options wrap or stack. Horizontal page overflow is prohibited.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Inline groups must transform before labels or targets become unusable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: fieldset with legend and native radio controls or an equivalent radiogroup
keyboard: Tab enters and exits the group according to the radio foundation behavior.
Arrow keys move among eligible options.
Space selects the focused option.
Disabled options cannot be selected.
focus: The selected or first eligible option receives the appropriate tab stop.
Every focused option has a visible focus indicator.
Validation does not reset the current selection.
announcements: Selected option and position in the set are exposed.
Group help and error are programmatically associated.
Disabled reasons are available when required.
aria: Prefer native fieldset, legend, and radio semantics where possible.
Use aria-describedby for group help and error.
Use aria-invalid on the group or relevant control according to the foundation.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Selected, disabled, invalid, and read-only meaning use control state, text, border, and semantics in addition to color.

content.minimum: One visible legend and at least two mutually exclusive options.
content.typical: Two to five options with concise labels and optional descriptions.
content.maximum: A small immediately scannable set. Larger sets require SelectField or a dedicated searchable control.
content.wrapping: Labels and descriptions wrap while the control remains aligned to the first line.
content.truncation: Option labels and material descriptions must not be truncated.
content.localization: Support expanded legend, options, descriptions, disabled reasons, and validation.
content.emptyBehavior: A group with fewer than two eligible options requires review; one fixed value may not require an interactive control.
content.technicalContent: Raw enum keys, option IDs, capability names, and backend descriptions are prohibited.

notes: A yes-or-no question may use RadioGroupField when the user must make an explicit mutually exclusive choice. An independent optional state normally uses CheckboxField.

SelectField.name: SelectField
SelectField.description: Canonical single-selection field for choosing one normalized value from a bounded option set through a native or approved custom select foundation.
capabilities: Collect one value from a bounded option set.
Present placeholder, groups, descriptions, disabled options, and an optional clear action.
Support controlled opening, selection, loading, empty-option, and dependency-error states.
Associate the select with visible label, help, and validation feedback.
Preserve keyboard navigation and focus behavior through an approved select foundation.
Prevent raw backend enums from becoming user-facing options.

foundation.source: Radix Select or native select, FormField, FieldHelp, FieldError
foundation.reason: Single-selection fields require normalized options, placeholder semantics, overlay focus management, disabled-option policy, loading and empty states, and clear boundaries from radio and searchable-combobox patterns.

standard.intent: Collect one value from an ordinary bounded option set.
prohibitedUse: Two or three options better compared as radios.
Large remotely searched entity collection.
Multiple selection.

nullable.intent: Allow a deliberate no-selection or none value in addition to the bounded options.
prohibitedUse: Required field.
Using placeholder as an ambiguous submitted value.
Conflating none with unknown or unavailable.

grouped.intent: Present a bounded option set divided into meaningful nonselectable groups.
prohibitedUse: Using groups only as decoration.
Deep hierarchy.
Large tree selection.
Groups whose labels expose backend structure.

dependent.intent: Present options whose availability depends on another already selected field or resolved prerequisite.
prohibitedUse: Fetching options directly inside SelectField.
Silently clearing an existing value without form reconciliation.
Displaying stale options as authoritative.

compact.intent: Dense bounded selection for filters or compact dialogs.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Visible field label.
contentRestrictions: Identify the value being selected.
Do not use the placeholder as the only label.

slots.name: trigger
slots.description: Approved select trigger showing placeholder or current selected label.
contentRestrictions: Must expose expanded, disabled, invalid, and current-value state.
Current value uses the normalized option label.

slots.name: placeholder
slots.description: Prompt shown before an eligible value is selected.
contentRestrictions: Use task-oriented text such as Selecione uma categoria.
Placeholder is not a hidden submitted value.
Required fields must not submit the placeholder.

slots.name: option
slots.description: One normalized selectable value.
contentRestrictions: Every option requires a stable value and user-facing label.
Raw backend enum keys are prohibited.
Disabled options require an understandable reason when relevant.

slots.name: optionDescription
slots.description: Optional concise supplementary option context.
contentRestrictions: Keep descriptions short.
If options require substantial comparison, use RadioGroupField or a dedicated picker.

slots.name: groupLabel
slots.description: Optional nonselectable heading for a meaningful option group.
contentRestrictions: Use user-facing categories.
Do not expose backend namespaces.

slots.name: clearAction
slots.description: Optional action clearing a nullable selection.
contentRestrictions: Allowed only when null is a valid form value.
Require an accessible label.

slots.name: help
slots.description: Optional persistent selection guidance.
contentRestrictions: Explain selection criteria or prerequisite.
Do not duplicate the selected option.

slots.name: state
slots.description: Loading, no-options, dependency-error, or unavailable option state.
contentRestrictions: Loading options, no eligible options, and failed option retrieval remain distinct.
State presentation must not be represented as a fake selectable option.

slots.name: error
slots.description: Current normalized field validation error.
contentRestrictions: Validation error remains separate from option-loading failure.

props.name: id
restrictions: Must be unique and stable.

props.name: name
restrictions: Maps to one selected value.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Nullable requires null to be an approved value.
Dependent requires external prerequisite ownership.

props.name: size
restrictions: The option overlay retains usable targets regardless of trigger density.

props.name: value
restrictions: Must match one normalized eligible option or null when permitted.
The visible option label is not used as the stable value.

props.name: onValueChange
restrictions: The callback updates form state and does not execute a mutation.

props.name: options
restrictions: Options require unique stable values.
Option order follows user task logic.
Very large or remotely searchable sets require a dedicated combobox or entity picker.
Multi-selection requires a separate component.

props.name: required
props.description: Indicates that one eligible non-null value is required.
restrictions: Must remain synchronized with validation.
Required fields must not allow clear.

props.name: disabled
restrictions: A dependency-disabled field requires visible prerequisite guidance when not obvious.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Indicates an invalid selected value or missing required selection.
restrictions: Requires an associated normalized FieldError.

props.name: loading
props.description: Indicates that the current option source is pending.
restrictions: Loading must not silently preserve options from an incompatible prerequisite.
The shared component does not fetch the options.

props.name: open
restrictions: Use controlled opening only when the owning workflow needs it.
Ordinary overlay state may remain foundation-owned.

props.name: onOpenChange
restrictions: Must remain paired with controlled open when supplied.

prohibitedChildren: SearchInput embedded as an improvised combobox
spacingOwnership: SelectField owns spacing among label, trigger, help, state, clear action, and error.
The select foundation owns overlay item spacing and positioning.
The form layout owns spacing around the complete field.
composition.surfaceOwnership: SelectField owns one trigger surface. The select foundation owns one elevated option overlay.
rules: One SelectField represents one selected value.
Options are normalized outside the shared component.
Placeholder, null, unknown, unavailable, and no eligible options remain distinct.
Few visible options may be better represented by RadioGroupField.
Large searchable sets require a dedicated combobox or entity picker.
The component does not fetch options.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for bounded single-selection fields.
Use for bounded filter values and preserve URL ownership outside the component.
Organization, role, policy, and integration options require normalized labels and eligibility.
Use for bounded classifications; final decisions with few consequential options may favor RadioGroupField.
Use only for genuine bounded authentication context such as organization selection.

notes: The owning form controls the selected value, validation, touched state, and dirty state.
Option data, dependency state, and eligibility remain feature- or query-owned.
Overlay disclosure may remain foundation-owned unless explicitly controlled.
The foundation manages trigger focus, overlay focus, and local overlay scrolling.
Value changes are emitted to the owning form.

responsive.strategy: Preserve the selected value, option labels, and overlay usability within the available viewport.
responsive.compact: The trigger fills the field width. The option overlay respects viewport margins and may use a constrained height.
responsive.medium: Use the expected-content width or form-grid width.
responsive.wide: Do not expand the trigger beyond the value's reasonable reading width.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Long option labels wrap or use an approved safe truncation policy. The overlay scrolls locally.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Trigger, options, descriptions, and actions remain usable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: native select or approved listbox-style select with a visible associated label
keyboard: Trigger opens with the foundation-supported keys.
Arrow keys move among eligible options.
Enter or Space selects according to foundation behavior.
Escape closes without changing the current value.
Typeahead behavior may be supported for the already loaded bounded option set.
focus: Opening moves focus according to the approved select foundation.
Closing restores focus to the trigger.
Validation does not clear the selected value.
Dependency updates do not unexpectedly move focus.
announcements: Expanded state, selected option, option count, disabled options, and invalid state are exposed.
Loading and option errors use canonical state semantics.
No-options state is not announced as a selectable option.
aria: Prefer native select semantics when product requirements permit.
Custom selects must follow the foundation listbox interaction contract.
Use aria-describedby for help, dependency context, and error.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Selected, expanded, disabled, invalid, loading, and unavailable meaning use text, control state, and semantics in addition to color.

content.minimum: One visible label, one select trigger, and at least one eligible normalized option or an explicit option state.
content.typical: Label, trigger, bounded options, optional help, and conditional error.
content.maximum: A bounded single-selection option set. Large, hierarchical, searchable, or multi-selection sets require another component.
content.wrapping: Labels, help, errors, and option descriptions wrap. Trigger text remains understandable.
content.truncation: Selected values must not truncate into ambiguity. Full option text remains available in the overlay.
content.localization: Support expanded labels, placeholders, options, group labels, disabled reasons, and errors.
content.emptyBehavior: No eligible options use a deliberate EmptyState or unavailable explanation rather than a disabled fake option.
content.technicalContent: Raw enum keys, IDs, query-state labels, API errors, and backend grouping names are prohibited.

notes: Searchable entity selection requires a dedicated ComboboxField or EntityPicker contract and must not be improvised by combining SearchInput with SelectField.
Multi-selection requires a separate component and value model.

TextareaField.name: TextareaField
TextareaField.description: Canonical multiline plain-text field for descriptions, notes, rationale, and bounded long-form input, with controlled resizing, character limits, validation, and accessible guidance.
capabilities: Collect plain multiline text.
Present default, rationale, notes, and long-form input variants.
Support fixed or bounded automatic height growth.
Integrate character-count feedback with authoritative validation limits.
Preserve user-entered content through validation and recoverable submission failures.
Associate the textarea with visible label, help, and normalized errors.

foundation.source: FormField, native textarea, FieldHelp, FieldError, CharacterCount
foundation.reason: Multiline input requires bounded resizing, content-purpose variants, validation preservation, character-limit alignment, and specific accessibility behavior beyond a generic input.

standard.intent: Collect an ordinary bounded multiline description.
prohibitedUse: Single short value better represented by Input.
Rich-text document editing.
Code editor.
Unbounded document content.

rationale.intent: Collect a human explanation supporting a consequential decision or review outcome.
prohibitedUse: Machine-generated explanation accepted as human rationale without review.
Optional decorative notes.
Hiding required evidence inside a free-text field.

notes.intent: Collect optional operational notes that supplement structured data.
prohibitedUse: Replacing structured fields with unsearchable free text.
Collecting secrets or sensitive credentials.
Required decision rationale.

longForm.intent: Collect a longer but still bounded plain-text response.
allowedUse: Structured narrative supported by visible guidance.
prohibitedUse: Rich text requiring headings, lists, or embedded media.
Unbounded document authoring.
Markdown editor without a dedicated preview and security contract.

compact.intent: Short multiline content in a constrained dialog or panel.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Visible field label.
contentRestrictions: Name the requested narrative or rationale.
Do not use placeholder text as the only label.

slots.name: control
slots.description: Native textarea control.
contentRestrictions: Plain text only unless another specialized editor contract exists.
The control must retain entered content through recoverable errors.

slots.name: help
slots.description: Optional persistent instruction, criteria, format, or privacy context.
contentRestrictions: Rationale fields should explain the expected decision evidence.
Do not require the user to infer expectations from placeholder examples alone.

slots.name: characterCount
slots.description: Optional authoritative character-count feedback.
contentRestrictions: Count limit must match the active client and server validation contract.
Do not announce every character typed.

slots.name: status
slots.description: Optional autosave, restored-draft, or pending-dependency context supplied by the owning workflow.
contentRestrictions: The shared field does not implement autosave.
Status must not obscure current validation.

slots.name: error
slots.description: Current normalized textarea validation error.
contentRestrictions: Explain required content, length, or field-specific business constraints.
Do not expose raw schema messages.

props.name: id
restrictions: Must be unique and stable.

props.name: name
restrictions: Maps to one plain-text value.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Rationale requires user-authored review or decision context.
Notes must not replace structured fields.

props.name: size
restrictions: Comfortable is reserved for higher-attention content.

props.name: value
restrictions: Must remain visible through validation and recoverable submission failures.
Do not normalize whitespace destructively while the user is typing.

props.name: onValueChange
restrictions: The callback updates form state and does not execute autosave or mutation directly.

props.name: required
props.description: Indicates that the active form contract requires a nonempty value.
restrictions: Must match validation.
Whitespace-only values require an explicit normalization policy.

props.name: minimumLength
restrictions: Must match the active schema.
Use only when minimum length meaningfully improves content quality.

props.name: maximumLength
restrictions: Must match client and server validation.
Required when CharacterCount is rendered.

props.name: minimumRows
restrictions: Must remain large enough to communicate multiline behavior.

props.name: maximumRows
props.description: Maximum automatic-growth rows before internal scrolling begins.
restrictions: Must be greater than or equal to minimumRows.
Unbounded page growth is prohibited.

props.name: autoResize
restrictions: Growth remains bounded by maximumRows.
Resizing must not cause disruptive page jumps.

props.name: disabled
restrictions: The reason should be available when not obvious.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Preserves visible selectable content while preventing editing.
restrictions: Ordinary non-form read-only narratives may use another data-display component.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Indicates that the current text violates the active field contract.
restrictions: Requires an associated FieldError.

spacingOwnership: TextareaField owns spacing among label, textarea, help, character count, status, and error.
The textarea owns its internal text padding and bounded scrolling.
The form layout owns spacing around the complete field.
composition.surfaceOwnership: TextareaField owns one textarea control surface and no additional card.
rules: The component collects plain text.
Character limits remain synchronized with validation.
Automatic growth remains bounded.
Recoverable validation and submission errors preserve entered content.
Autosave behavior belongs to the owning workflow.
Structured data should not be replaced by free-text notes.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for bounded multiline plain text.
Human rationale must remain editable, reviewable, and distinct from machine-generated recommendation text.
Use for descriptions, reasons, and bounded configuration notes.
Authentication should not normally require multiline free text.
Use SearchInput and structured filters.

prohibited: Running content moderation or validation requests directly.

notes: The owning form controls value, touched state, dirty state, validation, and submission mapping.
Draft persistence and autosave remain workflow-owned.
The textarea manages text-editing focus and local internal scrolling after reaching its maximum height.
No persistence side effect occurs inside the shared field.

responsive.strategy: Use the available field width, preserve readable line length, and bound vertical growth.
responsive.compact: Fill the field width and use the approved minimum rows. Supporting information stacks below.
responsive.medium: Use the form-grid width and bounded automatic resizing.
responsive.wide: Constrain long-form reading width even when the form section is wider.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not stretch long-form text across the complete route.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Text wraps natively. Internal vertical scrolling begins after maximumRows. Horizontal scrolling is prohibited for ordinary prose.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Label, text, count, status, and validation remain usable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: native textarea associated with a visible label
keyboard: Use native multiline text editing.
Tab follows project policy and normally moves focus rather than inserting a tab character.
Keyboard users can reach supporting links or actions separately.
focus: Validation and autosave status do not move focus.
Recoverable failures preserve selection and entered content where possible.
announcements: Help, character limits, and validation errors are associated with the textarea.
Character count is not announced for every keystroke.
Autosave status announcements are owned by FormStatus.
aria: Use aria-describedby for help, count, status, and error as appropriate.
Prefer native required, disabled, and read-only semantics.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Required, invalid, disabled, read-only, count-warning, and pending meaning use text and semantics in addition to color.

content.minimum: One visible label and one multiline text control.
content.typical: Label, textarea, help, optional character count, and conditional validation error.
content.maximum: A bounded plain-text response. Rich, structured, or document-length content requires another editor contract.
content.truncation: Editable content is never visually truncated.
content.localization: Support expanded labels, guidance, validation, counts, and status text.
content.emptyBehavior: Empty value is valid only when the field contract permits it.
content.technicalContent: Raw HTML, hidden markup, secrets, credentials, stack traces, and implementation configuration are prohibited unless the field explicitly collects safe technical content.

notes: Rich-text, code, markdown, and document editors require dedicated contracts, sanitization policies, keyboard models, and preview behavior.

DateField.name: DateField
DateField.description: Canonical single-value date field for date-only, month, or local date-time values, with explicit temporal semantics, calendar interaction, manual entry, localization, constraints, and timezone ownership.
capabilities: Collect one date-only, month, or local date-time value.
Support localized manual entry and an approved calendar picker.
Preserve an unambiguous canonical value at the form boundary.
Communicate minimum, maximum, unavailable, invalid, and dependency states.
Distinguish date-only values from instants and local wall-clock values.
Prevent accidental timezone conversion of date-only values.

foundation.source: FormField, native date inputs or approved calendar popover, Button, FieldHelp, FieldError
foundation.reason: Temporal input requires explicit value semantics, localization, parsing and formatting boundaries, calendar keyboard behavior, constraint validation, and timezone policy beyond a generic text field.

dateOnly.intent: Collect a calendar date that does not represent an instant or time of day.
prohibitedUse: Event timestamp.
Audit timestamp.
Server execution instant.
Converting the value through UTC before storage.

dateTimeLocal.intent: Collect a local wall-clock date and time whose timezone or zone context is supplied explicitly by the workflow.
allowedUse: Schedule an event in a known organization timezone.
Set a local deadline with explicit zone context.
Plan an operation in a selected location.
prohibitedUse: Storing an ambiguous local date-time without zone context.
Audit or system timestamps entered manually without a product requirement.
Assuming the browser timezone is always authoritative.

month.intent: Collect one calendar month without a specific day.
prohibitedUse: Fabricating the first day of the month as user-entered meaning.
Date ranges.
Precise timestamps.

dependent.intent: Collect a date whose valid range depends on another resolved form value.
prohibitedUse: Calculating business rules inside the shared component.
Silently changing the selected date when the dependency changes.
Using a single DateField to collect a complete date range.

compact.intent: Compact date control for filters or bounded dialogs.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Visible field label naming the temporal value.
contentRestrictions: Name the business meaning of the date.
Do not use placeholder text as the only label.

slots.name: input
slots.description: Manual date, month, or local date-time entry control.
contentRestrictions: Visible formatting follows locale while the canonical value remains unambiguous.
Date-only values must not be converted through UTC.

slots.name: calendarTrigger
slots.description: Optional action opening the approved calendar picker.
contentRestrictions: Require an accessible label.
Manual input must remain available when required by the product accessibility policy.

slots.name: calendar
slots.description: Optional calendar or month-picker overlay.
contentRestrictions: Disabled dates must be programmatically unavailable.
Month and year navigation must be keyboard operable.
The picker must not hide the active date constraints.

slots.name: timeControl
slots.description: Optional local time control for dateTimeLocal.
contentRestrictions: Allowed only for dateTimeLocal.
Use one consistent 12-hour or 24-hour locale policy.
Timezone context remains visible.

slots.name: timezoneContext
slots.description: Visible timezone or zone context for local date-time values.
contentRestrictions: Required for dateTimeLocal unless the product context makes the zone unambiguous.
Do not expose an internal timezone identifier without a user-facing label.

slots.name: help
slots.description: Optional persistent format, range, or business-rule guidance.
contentRestrictions: Explain minimum, maximum, excluded dates, or dependency where relevant.
Do not rely only on disabled calendar cells to communicate the rule.

slots.name: clearAction
slots.description: Optional action clearing a nullable date value.
contentRestrictions: Allowed only when null is a valid value.
Require an accessible label.

slots.name: error
slots.description: Current normalized date-field validation error.
contentRestrictions: Explain invalid format, range, dependency, or unavailable date in user-facing language.
Do not expose parser exceptions.

props.name: id
restrictions: Must be unique and stable.

props.name: name
restrictions: Maps to one canonical temporal value.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Variant must match the domain meaning.
Dependent retains the underlying date-only or local-date-time contract defined by the feature.

props.name: size
restrictions: Calendar targets retain the design-system minimum size.

props.name: value
restrictions: dateOnly uses YYYY-MM-DD.
month uses YYYY-MM.
dateTimeLocal uses an explicitly documented local date-time representation paired with zone context.
Do not pass JavaScript Date objects across the field boundary.
Null is allowed only when the field contract permits it.

props.name: onValueChange
restrictions: Manual entry and calendar selection emit the same canonical representation.
The callback does not convert date-only values to UTC.

props.name: minimum
restrictions: Must use the same temporal representation as value.
Must remain synchronized with validation.

props.name: maximum
restrictions: Must use the same temporal representation as value.
Must remain synchronized with validation.

props.name: required
props.description: Indicates that a valid temporal value is required.
restrictions: Must remain synchronized with validation.
Required fields must not expose clear behavior.

props.name: disabled
restrictions: The reason should be visible when not obvious.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Displays the canonical temporal value without allowing modification.
restrictions: Read-only date presentation outside a form may use DefinitionList or MetadataList.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Indicates invalid format, range, dependency, or temporal semantics.
restrictions: Requires an associated normalized FieldError.

props.name: timezone
props.description: Explicit IANA timezone or approved project timezone context for dateTimeLocal.
restrictions: Required when local date-time meaning depends on a zone.
Must not be inferred silently from the browser when the product has an authoritative zone.

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Externally supplied eligibility function for calendar dates.
restrictions: Business rules are resolved outside the shared component.
The function must remain deterministic for the rendered option set.
Disabled dates require visible rule guidance when not obvious.

prohibitedChildren: Second date field forming an undocumented range
Timezone selector without a product contract
spacingOwnership: DateField owns spacing among label, input, calendar trigger, timezone context, help, clear action, and error.
The calendar foundation owns overlay layout and date-grid spacing.
The form layout owns spacing around the complete field.
composition.surfaceOwnership: DateField owns one input or grouped temporal-control surface. The calendar foundation owns one elevated picker surface.
rules: Temporal semantics are selected before implementation.
Date-only values never become instants implicitly.
Local date-time requires explicit zone context.
Manual entry and picker selection share one canonical value contract.
Date ranges require a dedicated range composition.
Business-day and availability rules remain feature-owned.

libraries: date-fns or approved project date utility

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for explicit single temporal values.
Single date filters may use DateField; ranges require a dedicated range composition.
Activation, expiration, and scheduling require explicit zone and constraint policies.
Review deadlines and effective dates require explicit temporal meaning.
Use only for a genuine authentication requirement such as date of birth, following privacy policy.

prohibited: Reading browser timezone as authoritative without a policy.

notes: The owning form controls canonical value, validation, touched state, dirty state, and submission mapping.
The feature supplies temporal semantics, timezone, range constraints, and date eligibility.
Calendar overlay disclosure may remain foundation-owned.
The calendar foundation manages local focus and overlay scrolling.
Value changes are emitted without persistence or transport conversion.

responsive.strategy: Preserve temporal meaning, complete formatted value, calendar navigation, and timezone context within the viewport.
responsive.compact: The input fills the field width. Calendar overlay uses viewport margins and appropriately sized date targets. Time controls stack.
responsive.medium: Use expected-content width with visible timezone context where required.
responsive.wide: Keep input width aligned to the temporal format rather than stretching indefinitely.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Labels, help, zone context, and errors wrap. Calendar overlays scroll or reposition locally without page overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Manual input, calendar navigation, dates, time controls, and errors remain operable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: native date-related input or labeled composite date field with an accessible dialog-style calendar
keyboard: Manual entry follows native text or date-input behavior.
Calendar trigger is keyboard operable.
Calendar navigation follows the approved date-picker keyboard model.
Escape closes the picker and restores focus to the trigger.
Disabled dates cannot be selected.
focus: Opening the picker moves focus to the selected date, current date, or first eligible date according to the foundation policy.
Closing restores focus to the trigger.
Validation does not clear the current value.
Dependency changes do not unexpectedly move focus.
announcements: Selected date, visible month, disabled dates, range constraints, invalid state, and timezone context are perceivable.
aria: Use native temporal input semantics where appropriate.
Composite calendar implementations require an accessible dialog and date-grid contract.
Use aria-describedby for help, zone context, and error.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Selected, current, unavailable, disabled, invalid, required, and out-of-range dates use text, shape, semantics, or icons in addition to color.

content.minimum: One visible label and one temporal input.
content.typical: Label, input, optional calendar picker, visible constraints, and conditional validation error.
content.maximum: One date, month, or local date-time value. Ranges and scheduling workflows require dedicated compositions.
content.wrapping: Labels, zone context, guidance, and validation wrap naturally.
content.truncation: Formatted values and timezone context must not truncate into ambiguity.
content.localization: Support localized display, manual-entry guidance, month names, weekday names, time format, and validation while retaining a canonical machine value.
content.emptyBehavior: Empty value is valid only when the active contract permits null.
content.technicalContent: Raw Date objects, epoch values, parser exceptions, UTC conversion details, and transport formats are prohibited in ordinary presentation.

notes: A DateRangeField requires a separate contract covering start and end values, range ordering, inclusive or exclusive semantics, range presets, and two-field validation.
Instant timestamps are generally produced by the system rather than manually entered through DateField.

checks.description: The form-field control catalog must validate against the component catalog schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid or missing specialized-control fields.

checks.description: Specialized field IDs, names, implementations, public imports, and canonical responsibilities must remain unique.
checks.remediation: Resolve duplicate ownership or merge overlapping form-control contracts.

checks.description: Shared specialized controls must not execute queries, mutations, persistence, permission checks, enum mapping, temporal business rules, or transport conversion.
checks.remediation: Move data access, domain mapping, eligibility, temporal policy, and persistence to the owning form, feature, query, or route.

checks.description: CheckboxField, RadioGroupField, and SelectField must be selected according to the value model and option-set characteristics rather than visual preference.
checks.remediation: Replace the control with the canonical field matching boolean, small exclusive-choice, or bounded compacted-selection semantics.

checks.description: Checkbox and radio controls must expose native-equivalent label, checked, mixed, selected, required, disabled, invalid, and keyboard semantics.
checks.remediation: Correct label association, fieldset semantics, checked state, arrow-key behavior, focus, required state, or validation relationships.

checks.description: SelectField must preserve accessible single-selection behavior, focus restoration, normalized options, placeholder semantics, and state distinction.
checks.remediation: Correct select foundation behavior, option normalization, overlay focus, clear behavior, or loading and empty states.

checks.description: Consent checkboxes must not be preselected and must not combine unrelated agreements.
checks.remediation: Initialize consent as unchecked and divide distinct agreements into independently labeled fields.

checks.description: SelectField must not be used as an improvised searchable entity picker, multi-select, tree selector, or remote combobox.
checks.remediation: Create or select the dedicated control contract required by the option model.

checks.description: TextareaField character limits and validation constraints must remain synchronized with the authoritative form schema and server contract.
checks.remediation: Pass limits from the authoritative field contract and preserve entered content through recoverable failures.

checks.description: Date-only, month, local date-time, instant, and date-range semantics must not be conflated.
checks.remediation: Select an explicit temporal value contract and use a dedicated range or scheduling composition when necessary.

checks.description: DateField must preserve canonical values, avoid implicit UTC conversion of date-only values, and expose accessible picker behavior.
checks.remediation: Correct canonical representation, timezone ownership, parsing, formatting, range validation, keyboard navigation, or focus restoration.

checks.description: Specialized form controls must remain labeled, operable, correctly associated, and free from page-level overflow across approved viewports, zoom levels, and keyboard scenarios.
checks.remediation: Correct option stacking, overlay dimensions, textarea growth, calendar positioning, label wrapping, target size, or focus behavior.

checks.description: Page-local checkbox fields, radio-card groups, selects, textareas, and date pickers similar to canonical components require review.
checks.remediation: Reuse the canonical specialized field or document why the local implementation requires a distinct contract.
